answer: The naive web-of-trust trusts every edge forever. Decay it instead: an edge loses weight each epoch the pair does not re-attest, uptime unlocks the weight back, and a quorum counts only if it spans unrelated subnetworks. A whisper of collusion between two keys fades on its own. An attacker then needs a gale of fresh attestations every epoch across separate networks, and timber for a thousand identities means a thousand live connections, not a thousand keys.
